title: Token emission starvation: urgent hotfix for heterogeneous warmup + burst suppression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers reported sudden increases in TTFT and sustained drop in tokens/sec across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Root symptoms are 'token emission starvation' after large heterogeneous request bursts where warmup credit accounting and the burst-suppression shim interacted poorly with kernel selection, causing stalled emitter pipelines and delayed first-token times. This ticket coordinates a rapid fix, deployment canaries, and follow-up tests and telemetry to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: Interaction between three subsystems: (1) burst-suppression shim that clamps concurrent emitter windows based on recent token rates, (2) warmup-credit allocator that prioritizes steady-state fairness across tenants, and (3) kernel selector heuristic that deprioritizes kernels for requests with atypical batch shape. Under heterogeneous bursts (mixture of very long and short contexts) the allocator withheld warmup credits while the mirror kernel selector routed many long-context requests to a non-ideal kernel, causing KV-prefetch queues to pile up and token emission to stall. The combined effect produced high TTFT and low sustained tokens/sec across models with long prefix lengths.
mitigations: Immediate: Roll back kernel-selector heuristic change from runtime-1.18 -> deployed to canary nodes (reverts misprioritization of heterogeneous batches).
Immediate: Add an inflight KV-prefetch watermark that pauses new prefetch requests for overloaded workers instead of letting queues grow unbounded.
Short-term: Apply a transient warmup credit top-up for tenants exhibiting emission starvation (canary then staged rollout).
Short-term: Relax burst-suppression clamp thresholds in Dedicated APAC region to avoid over-throttling mixed-shaped workloads.
Medium-term: Add an explicit per-model warmup credit budget tied to observed long-context request ratios and expose override via Dedicated/Private config.
Medium-term: Harden kernel selection tests (see testing_and_validation) and add regression alerting for tokens/sec variance > 35% versus baseline for a model shard.
rollback_plan: If canary shows regression after selector rollback and KV-watermark, revert to previous runtime on canary and re-enable the conservative burst-suppressor while we iterate. Rolling back is low-risk for hosted; for Dedicated/Private we will coordinate with customer SREs and use staged traffic cutover to minimize disruption.
testing_and_validation: End-to-end synthetic harness with mixed request shapes (1x long-context 8k + 20x short 64-token) replicated 10k cycles to reproduce issue deterministically.
Add unit tests for kernel-selector scoring that include heterogeneous-batch heuristics and ensure per-shape priority is preserved.
Create telemetry regression test: deploy canary, run 30m workload, assert TTFT drop < 15% and tokens/sec within 90-110% of baseline.
Update Grafana dashboards to surface 'KV-prefetch queue depth' and 'warmup-credit balance per-tenant' for quick triage.
